verdict.rationale: Zulip's docs say every conversation in a channel lives in its own named topic. Subscribed channels feed the inbox and recent-conversations views, and multiple community users credit the topic model with letting them follow busy, many-participant discussions without being overwhelmed. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the topic-level catch-up workflow itself (e.g. reading or marking read per topic within the inbox or recent conversations).

support.subject: As a team-admin, I can catch up on busy channels efficiently because every conversation is organized under a named topic or thread

citations.quote: Lots of conversations can happen in the same channel at the same time, each in its own topic. You never have to worry about interrupting — each conversation has its own space.
Subscribing to a channel makes conversations in that channel appear in your inbox, recent conversations, combined feed and left sidebar.
It lets us have real, ongoing, and substantive conversations with a large number of participants without being overwhelmed.
